Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

success noun

doing or getting what one aimed at

also succeed, be a success, it worked, it didn’t work, without success, come off

classical

Ter. And. 670: hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā
Caes. BG 7.26.1: quod rēs nūlla successerat

succēdō, succēdere, successī, successum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive; what is attempted is the subject, the person in the dative

turn out well, succeed, work

Rēs mihi succēdit, it is going well for me; sī ex sententiā successerit, if it turns out as we wish (Cic. Q. fr. 2.14.1, Lewis & Short). In Plautus and Terence the compound has only this sense (de Vaan 103, s.v. cēdō).

Other words

  • rem bene gerere — succeed, do well (of a person)

    phrase: gerō with rem and an adverb (bene, prosperē, fēlīciter) · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 936: bene ambulā, bene rem gerās; Traupman 188, 387: success, rēs fēlīciter gesta, rēs bene gesta; M-O s.v. succeed: rem prosperē (fēlīciter) gessī

    Of someone who brings off what he set about, in business or in war. For how well someone does, see performance.

  • 1successus: short e (Traupman 387 succēssus). Lewis & Short leaves the vowel unmarked, as in suc-cēdo, cessi, cessum. After a long vowel ss was reduced to s in Augustan spelling (Quint. 1.7.20 records Cicero’s and Virgil’s caussae, cassus, divissiones), but cessī, cessum and successus kept ss, so the vowel before it is short.

    successus1, successūs m. — success, a happy outcome

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 42.66.3: ēlātus successū; Phaedr. 2.3.7: successus improbōrum plūrēs allicit

    Lewis & Short: “a happy issue, good result, success (the usual signif.; perh. not ante-Aug.)”: Virgil, Livy, Ovid, Phaedrus, Quintilian, Tacitus; not Cicero’s word.

  • rē īnfectā — without success, with nothing achieved

    phrase: ablative absolute · also used · classical · Liv. 42.16.4: rē īnfectā rediērunt; Caes. BG 7.17.5 (Lewis & Short)

    Literally “the thing not done”; also īnfectīs rēbus (Sallust, Nepos).

  • rēs bene (fēlīciter) gesta — a success, something well done

    also used · classical · Traupman 387

Examples

  • Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.

    I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out. … That way didn’t work; we’ll go at it another way.Ter. And. 669–670

  • Bene ambulā, bene rem gerās.

    Safe journey, and success to you.Plaut. Mil. 936

  • successus improbōrum plūrēs allicit

    the success of the wicked draws more people inPhaedr. 2.3.7

See also result, win, good luck!, approach, performance, successful.
